text:
maria: FYI support > brightio escalation - multiple 504s and 5xxs during a spike this morning starting ~08:23 UTC. Customer reports request timeouts and gateway failures when they ramped traffic.

ops-bot: Alert: high 5xx rate detected on hosted-gateway (org=brightio) — rate 18% over 5m :warning:

maria: Pasting the snippet customer provided (they captured curl + gateway log):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hello"}' --max-time 15
* curl: (28) Operation timed out after 15000 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
gateway: 2026-03-17T08:24:12Z ERROR request failed status=504 route=/v1/generate tenant=brightio
```

ashwin: Any ASG/HPA/KEDA events? can someone dump the scaler/pod events for brightio's serving pool?

lara: From cluster events (copying key lines):
```
Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  2m (x3 over 10m)  HorizontalPodAutoscaler  Scaled up replica set serving-brightio-78f -> 4
Warning BackOff             1m                   kubelet                  Back-off restarting failed container
Warning  Unhealthy           1m                   kubelet                  Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
Normal   ScaledObjectBackoff 30s                   keda-operator            ScaledObject brightio-queue backoff: cooldown 60s
```
This looks like KEDA observed high queue and scaled, but new pods are failing readiness/startup (model init timeouts). pods start but readiness probe fails repeatedly.

sam: Two likely contributors: (1) model cold-start/initialization exceeds startupProbe timeout, (2) KEDA/HPA control loop backoff and cooldown causes scaling to oscillate and not sustain capacity during surge. Also seen cases where KEDA polls at 30s and HPA hasn't caught up so requests queue up.

zoe: Customer says they saw auth 401s earlier but those cleared; current 5xxs are purely gateway/timeouts. I asked for a trace id; they gave: trace=brt-20260317-08-24-9ab3

maria: Repro steps I ran against staging tenant-brightio:
1) Run a small load: `hey -n 500 -c 30 https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
2) Observe spike -> queue length rises -> keda ScaledObject triggers new pods -> new pods stuck initializing for ~45-70s
3) Gateway returns 504s while queue drains

ashwin: Commands I'm running to inspect:
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l tenant=brightio -o wide
kubectl -n prod describe pod serving-brightio-6789
kubectl -n prod logs serving-brightio-6789 -c runtime
kubectl -n prod get scaledobject brightio-queue -o yaml
```

lara: Observed model init logs show repeated timeouts in the first 60s during weight mount and kv-cache restore. Example: `model:init timed out waiting for shard 0` then grace restart. StartupProbe is set to failureThreshold=10 periodSeconds=3 (30s) which is too low for large models on cold start.

sam: Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Increase replica minimum for brightio serving pool to 3 (manual scale) to avoid cold starts on small surges.
- Increase startupProbe failureThreshold to 40 (-> ~120s) and readiness initialDelaySeconds to 30 for the tenant serving pod spec.
- Lower KEDA `cooldownPeriod` and `pollingInterval` for this ScaledObject (e.g. pollingInterval: 10s, cooldownPeriod: 20s) to make scaler reactive (tradeoff: more control churn).
- Add a pre-warm job that hits `/internal/warmup` on new pods immediately after start to populate KV cache faster.

lara: Long-term fixes:
- Add a model-init readiness gating that reports progressive health (warm cache vs fully ready) so gateway can route degraded requests to older pool while new pods warm.
- Adjust default startupProbe for large-model tenants and expose as tenant-level config in Dedicated/Private.
- Evaluate vertical pod sizes for this workload or container image optimizations to shorten model load time (async snapshot restore, lazy weight load).

zoe: Customer-facing notes for BrightIo:
"We're investigating a scale-up delay that caused requests to time out during your traffic spike. We're applying a targeted mitigation (raising minimum replicas & probe timeouts) and will follow up when we've validated stability. We'll also run a warm-up for your model to clear prefix cache. Apologies for the disruption." :pray:

maria: I'm going to apply the short-term changes now in prod for brightio as a targeted rollbackable change (will annotate in deploy):
- `kubectl scale deploy serving-brightio --replicas=3`
- patch startupProbe: `failureThreshold: 40`
- patch ScaledObject pollingInterval -> 10s cooldownPeriod -> 20s

ashwin: I'll own post-mortem and action items. Next steps: collect metrics for the next 4h: pod init time distribution, 5xx rate, queue length, KEDA scale events. Assign to @ashwin for PM.

sam: Quick note: when applying probe changes, keep canary to one AZ first to avoid simultaneous model loads across all racks.

maria: Change applied to prod canary (cluster-a). Monitoring: 5xx rate dropped to 2% and new pods finished init in ~95s after increased startup window. Will continue to monitor.

ops-bot: Incident annotated: incident/brightio-scaleup-504-2612345678 created, severity=high, owner=ashwin

zoe: I'll send the customer a status update and schedule a post-mortem call for tomorrow.

ashwin: Thanks everyone. Logging follow-up tasks in the infra backlog and will include suggested defaults for large-model tenants.

maria: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see regression. :white_check_mark:
